## Subagent rows tell the truth about time and life

- **A resident child no longer shows a time.** `23s ago · resident` was showing when the child last wrote its status file — not an age of anything you did, and it read as though the child had just finished something. Resident and parent-waiting rows now just name the state. Rows for children that are actually working keep their age, where it does mean something: the time since their last activity, next to the tool they are running.

- **Children of a closed Pi no longer look alive.** After restarting PiTTy, some rows said `resident` and others did not, even though every one of them was inactive. A child cannot outlive the Pi process that spawned it — but its heartbeat stays fresh for up to two minutes after that process dies, and for that window its rows still looked live. PiTTy now also checks that the process which owns the child's control directory still exists (the pid is part of the directory name), so those children read `unresponsive` immediately and consistently instead of a mix.

  This closes the gap for children of a dead Pi. It does not replace the heartbeat — that still bounds liveness, and a recycled pid can only make the check briefly optimistic.
